stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu drenches Chennai, north T.N.; south T.N. next in line for heavy rainfall
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu drenches Chennai, north T.N.; south T.N. next in line for heavy rainfall
stories.summary: However, rainfall intensity is expected to reduce from Tuesday (November 3) after the system makes landfall
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu drenched the extreme northern parts of the State, including Chennai, from Sunday (November 1) evening, as the region lies along its path.
However, rainfall intensity is expected to reduce from Tuesday after the system makes landfall.
Cyclone Murasu (meaning percussion instrument in Tamil) followed close on the heels of Cyclone Arnab, and is also headed towards Andhra Pradesh coast.
It is likely to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur between Monday midnight and the early hours of Tuesday.

As the outer bands of the cyclone brushed along the Tamil Nadu north coastal region, the Regional Meteorological Centre upgraded its weather alerts for a few north TN districts like Chennai and Tiruvallur on Monday.
However, the rainfall intensity may drop to moderate in north Tamil Nadu from Tuesday.
Heavy downpours had lashed several areas in and around Chennai, particularly northern parts of the city during the past 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Monday.
Kadapakkam and Parrys corner in Chennai topped the charts with a very heavy rainfall of 15 cm each.
This was followed by many rain gauges, including Manali and Sathangadu, with 13 cm each.
Intermittent spells of rains continued through Monday as the cyclone inched closer to the Indian coast.
It would be the turn of south Tamil Nadu to receive heavy rainfall from November 5 with monsoon winds gaining strength.
While Theni and Dindigul are expected to receive heavy rainfall on November 5, nine districts, including Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Ramanathapuram, may record heavy rainfall till November 7.

stories.headline: WTA Chennai Open: New year, same damp squib as Cyclone Murasu washes out day 1
stories.title: WTA Chennai Open: New year, same damp squib as Cyclone Murasu washes out day 1
stories.summary: The weather in Chennai and the city’s susceptibility to cyclonic activity at this time of year vindicates WTA’s decision to relocate India’s only Tour-level event to the Philippines in 2027.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Rains brought in by cyclone Murasu led to a complete washout on the opening day of the WTA 250 Chennai Open at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam.

The intermittent drizzle, along with a brief downpour, forced the tournament organisers to eventually call the day off around 6:40 p.m. soon after they had issued a revised order of play which featured just five singles matches.
“Between 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. on Monday, the Nungambakkam area received 8.8mm of rainfall,” an India Meteorological Department (IMD) official told Sportstar.
Therefore, the action on Tuesday, featuring all 16 first-round matches, has been brought forward by four hours and will begin at 11 a.m. to get the tournament back on schedule.
However, according to IMD, thunderstorms and lightning are expected on Day 2 as well.
The first edition of the tournament was held in 2022 in September, the week following the U.S. Open, amidst clear skies.
But when it returned to India in November last year, the first two days of the main draw were completely washed out due to rain.
The same is likely to happen this time as well, vindicating WTA’s decision to relocate India’s only Tour-level event to the Philippines in 2027.
Of course, the growing popularity of Filipino star Alexandra Eala is the bigger factor behind the move.
As per Tuesday’s schedule, all three Indian wild cards - Vaishnavi Adkar, Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi and Sahaja Yamalapalli - will play one after the other on the Centre Court.

World No. 334 Vaishnavi, the top-ranked Indian, will be up against Jodie Burrage, the 27-year-old Brit who has entered the main draw via a Protected Ranking of 149 but has been ranked as high as 85th in the world.

After the 21-year-old Vaishnavi, Maaya will step on the court where the 17-year-old girl from Coimbatore, who recently clinched her maiden title at the senior level, will face Polish World No. 106 Katarzyna Kawa.

stories.headline: ‘Bada pataka’ under the counter, fake green labels on display: Banned firecrackers flood Delhi markets after Supreme Court nod
stories.title: ‘Bada pataka’ under the counter, fake green labels on display: Banned firecrackers flood Delhi markets after Supreme Court nod
stories.summary: The Hindu finds rockets, bombs and flowerpots sold discreetly in Sadar Bazar and Jama Masjid, with some green-labelled crackers lacking QR codes; vendors cite demand for louder fireworks as police seize over 1,100 kg
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Hours after the Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers were being openly sold, albeit discreetly, in Old Delhi’s Sadar Bazar and Jama Masjid markets.

A visit by The Hindu found vendors concealing banned crackers in cartons and black polythene bags beneath displays of green-labelled fireworks, with some selling conventional crackers without the QR codes required to verify their authenticity.
At least 10 vendors approached by The Hindu said traditional firecrackers, referred to in the market as “bada pataka”, were available.

One vendor opened his phone to show photographs of rockets, bombs, flowerpots and ground spinners, along with their prices, and said the items selected by a customer could be brought from a nearby warehouse in “five minutes”.

stories.headline: Three AAP leaders join BJP ahead of Punjab Assembly election
stories.title: Three AAP leaders join BJP ahead of Punjab Assembly election
stories.summary: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap, Sanour MLA Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Samana MLA Chetan Singh Jauramajra join the BJP in Delhi; State BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon says it indicates the impending end of the party’s regime in Punjab
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Monday (November 2, 2026) suffered a setback ahead of the Punjab Assembly election, due in early 2027, after three of its leaders — Kunwar Vijay Pratap, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jauramajra — joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in New Delhi.
Sanour MLA Mr. Pathanmajra and Samana MLA Mr. Jauramajra resigned from the party’s primary membership on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
They both said they were quitting the AAP as it had failed to fulfil the promises it had made ahead of the 2022 Assembly election.
Amritsar North MLA Mr. Pratap, a former Indian.
Police Service officer, resigned as a legislator on Monday (November 2, 2026) morning to join the BJP later in the day.
“There is an atmosphere of chaos all around Punjab.
Drug abuse has reached alarming levels and a drug empire has been established.
Extortion has now become an industry, and gangsterism is also at its peak,” Mr. Pratap said after joining the BJP.

Mr. Pratap has remained critical of the government’s handling of various sensitive issues, including the sluggish investigation into alleged incidents of the desecration of the Guru Granth Sahib and subsequent police firings at Behbal Kalan in Faridkot district that claimed the lives of two Sikh protesters in 2015.
He has also questioned the AAP’s touted ‘Schools of Eminence’.

In 2023, ahead of AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal’s visit to inaugurate Punjab’s first School of Eminence in Amritsar, Mr. Pratap had pointed out that the school in question had only been “renovated”, and that it had been made a smart school by the previous governments.
In June 2025, Mr. Pratap was suspended from the party for five years for indulging in anti-party activities.

stories.headline: Why articulate storytellers will outshine future AI
stories.title: Why articulate storytellers will outshine future AI
stories.summary: Twelve years ago, top guys from Bain & Company, the global consultancy firm, spent time with Nand Kishore Chaudhary of Jaipur Rugs and his weavers in a Rajasthan village. At the end of the visit, they told Chaudhary there were thousands of “authentic” stories to be told about him and his company.Recounting this in the anniversary issue of your magazine earlier this year, my colleague Pankti Mehta Kadakia wrote that this left Chaudhary in a daze. “We sell carpets,” he told the folks from Bain.Naturally, when we hosted Chaudhary at Forbes India Leadership Circuit in Jaipur on October 23, it felt most natural to steer the conversation towards his stories.Not content to run the shoe shop in Churu his father owned, Chaudhary joined a bank in Jaipur as a cashier before finding his feet in carpets. Starting with a ₹5,000 loan from his father, he wove a story unlike any other. Curiously for a company whose identity is luxury, Jaipur Rugs works with thousands on the margins. To have more women weaving for his company—Chaudhary did not find men to be too reliable—he decentralised his model. Instead of getting people to the factory, he took the factory to the people by shipping raw material to them however remote their villages were.Early in his career, Chaudhary was often told he was a good human being but that made him a bad businessman. Today, the story of Jaipur Rugs—perched comfortably on the cusp of a luxury brand and a social effort—is the answer to those Cassandras. The best thing about this story is the manner in which Chaudhary tells it: Simply.As does Rajesh Maheshwari, who started ALLEN Career Institute in 1988 teaching eight students at his family home in Kota. This was forced by family circumstances. Left to himself, Maheshwari, a diploma holder in mechanical engineering, would have liked nothing better than to drive trains running between Mumbai and Kota.Instead, he has seen more than 4.4 million students pass through ALLEN’s coaching facilities and employs hundreds of IIT grads as teachers. Finally, teachers in India, accustomed to getting more respect in society than money from employers, are earning annual salaries running into crores.The story was compelling enough for Bodhi Tree Systems, led by James Murdoch and Uday Shankar, to invest $600 million in ALLEN valuing it at well above $1 billion four years ago, as the world was still taking ginger steps out of the Covid-19 pandemic. That was also the time when edtech companies began to face existential questions with the return of students to classrooms.Somewhere in there is another story about the primacy of the human touch—something you will hear from global tech luminaries in this issue of your magazine. That should surprise no one.In my infrequent meetings with tech honchos, I make it a point to ask which skills they value the most in their people at a time when artificial intelligence (AI) is taking over many of the tasks traditionally performed by humans. The most frequent answers list two skills.One is the ability to take up complex subjects and articulate them in a way that is easy to understand for everyone. The second is the ability to tell a story.The latter, as scores of management journals have established, adds a warm and fuzzy element to the way a brand is perceived, making consumers prefer it to those that have no stories to tell. And the former matters because, well, if you are going to tell a story, best to tell it simply.Suveen SinhaEditor, Forbes IndiaEmail: suveen.sinha@nw18.comX ID: @suveensinha

opening: Twelve years ago, top guys from Bain & Company, the global consultancy firm, spent time with Nand Kishore Chaudhary of Jaipur Rugs and his weavers in a Rajasthan village.
At the end of the visit, they told Chaudhary there were thousands of “authentic” stories to be told about him and his company.
body: Recounting this in the anniversary issue of your magazine earlier this year, my colleague Pankti Mehta Kadakia wrote that this left Chaudhary in a daze.
“We sell carpets,” he told the folks from Bain.
Naturally, when we hosted Chaudhary at Forbes India Leadership Circuit in Jaipur on October 23, it felt most natural to steer the conversation towards his stories.
Not content to run the shoe shop in Churu his father owned, Chaudhary joined a bank in Jaipur as a cashier before finding his feet in carpets.
Starting with a ₹5,000 loan from his father, he wove a story unlike any other.
Curiously for a company whose identity is luxury, Jaipur Rugs works with thousands on the margins.
To have more women weaving for his company—Chaudhary did not find men to be too reliable—he decentralised his model.
Instead of getting people to the factory, he took the factory to the people by shipping raw material to them however remote their villages were.
Early in his career, Chaudhary was often told he was a good human being but that made him a bad businessman.
Today, the story of Jaipur Rugs—perched comfortably on the cusp of a luxury brand and a social effort—is the answer to those Cassandras.
The best thing about this story is the manner in which Chaudhary tells it: Simply.
As does Rajesh Maheshwari, who started ALLEN Career Institute in 1988 teaching eight students at his family home in Kota.
This was forced by family circumstances.
Left to himself, Maheshwari, a diploma holder in mechanical engineering, would have liked nothing better than to drive trains running between Mumbai and Kota.
Instead, he has seen more than 4.4 million students pass through ALLEN’s coaching facilities and employs hundreds of IIT grads as teachers.
Finally, teachers in India, accustomed to getting more respect in society than money from employers, are earning annual salaries running into crores.

The story was compelling enough for Bodhi Tree Systems, led by James Murdoch and Uday Shankar, to invest $600 million in ALLEN valuing it at well above $1 billion four years ago, as the world was still taking ginger steps out of the Covid-19 pandemic.
That was also the time when edtech companies began to face existential questions with the return of students to classrooms.
Somewhere in there is another story about the primacy of the human touch—something you will hear from global tech luminaries in this issue of your magazine.
That should surprise no one.

In my infrequent meetings with tech honchos, I make it a point to ask which skills they value the most in their people at a time when artificial intelligence (AI) is taking over many of the tasks traditionally performed by humans.
The most frequent answers list two skills.
One is the ability to take up complex subjects and articulate them in a way that is easy to understand for everyone.
The second is the ability to tell a story.
The latter, as scores of management journals have established, adds a warm and fuzzy element to the way a brand is perceived, making consumers prefer it to those that have no stories to tell.
And the former matters because, well, if you are going to tell a story, best to tell it simply.
Suveen SinhaEditor, Forbes IndiaEmail: suveen.sinha@nw18.comX ID: @suveensinha.

stories.headline: Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness, weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in Kishtwar
stories.title: Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness, weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in Kishtwar
stories.summary: Kishtwar, Nov 2: Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year. Addressing the gathering, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the India Meteorology Department (IMD) had strengthened the weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban. Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, Senior Scientist Suresh and others came specially from Delhi for the event. MLA Padder-Nagseni Constituency and Leader of Opposition, J&K Legislative Assembly, Sunil Sharma; MLA of the Kishtwar Assembly Constituency and Shagun Parihar also spoke on the occasion. Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Sharma and SSP Kishtwar Sunny Gupta were also present among others. The Minister said, the expansion of scientific and weather monitoring infrastructure has also strengthened the region's disaster preparedness in an area that is vulnerable to earthquakes, landslides and other weather-related challenges. The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi. With the establishment of the new facility, Jammu and Kashmir now has four Seismological Observatories, including those at Jammu, Srinagar, Udhampur and Kishtwar. Dr Jitendra Singh said the observatory would continuously monitor earthquake activity in the region and contribute to a better understanding of its seismic hazards. The information generated would also support the district administration and rescue teams in responding more effectively, besides helping in planning safer infrastructure. Highlighting the transformation in meteorological infrastructure since 2014, Dr Jitendra Singh said that there was no Doppler Weather Radar coverage in the region earlier. After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities. He further informed that four more Doppler Weather Radars are set to be commissioned in 2027 at Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla, further strengthening weather surveillance and extending coverage across the region. The Minister also highlighted the significant expansion of the Automatic Weather Station network. From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12. These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua. Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region. He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas. The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency. These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring. Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts. The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information. He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir. The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services. Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness. Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease. Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon. He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings. “Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories. Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication. He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources. Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas. He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them. Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub. He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people. The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

opening: Kishtwar, Nov 2: Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the India Meteorology Department (IMD) had strengthened the weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban.
body: Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, Senior Scientist Suresh and others came specially from Delhi for the event.
MLA Padder-Nagseni Constituency and Leader of Opposition, J&K Legislative Assembly, Sunil Sharma; MLA of the Kishtwar Assembly Constituency and Shagun Parihar also spoke on the occasion.
Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Sharma and SSP Kishtwar Sunny Gupta were also present among others.

The Minister said, the expansion of scientific and weather monitoring infrastructure has also strengthened the region's disaster preparedness in an area that is vulnerable to earthquakes, landslides and other weather-related challenges.

The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi.
With the establishment of the new facility, Jammu and Kashmir now has four Seismological Observatories, including those at Jammu, Srinagar, Udhampur and Kishtwar.
Dr Jitendra Singh said the observatory would continuously monitor earthquake activity in the region and contribute to a better understanding of its seismic hazards.
The information generated would also support the district administration and rescue teams in responding more effectively, besides helping in planning safer infrastructure.
Highlighting the transformation in meteorological infrastructure since 2014, Dr Jitendra Singh said that there was no Doppler Weather Radar coverage in the region earlier.
After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities.

He further informed that four more Doppler Weather Radars are set to be commissioned in 2027 at Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla, further strengthening weather surveillance and extending coverage across the region.
The Minister also highlighted the significant expansion of the Automatic Weather Station network.
From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12.
These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region.
He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas.
The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency.
These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring.
Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts.
The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information.
He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir.
The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness.
Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease.
Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon.
He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings.
“Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories.
Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication.
He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources.

Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas.
He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them.
Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub.
He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people.
The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid, rehabilitation for rescued bonded labourers
stories.title: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid, rehabilitation for rescued bonded labourers
stories.summary: Bench says eradication of bonded labour is a “continuing obligation”, requiring authorities to ensure that those freed are meaningfully rehabilitated
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Observing that the state’s constitutional obligation towards bonded labourers does not end with their release, the Supreme Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) asked the Centre to lay down a uniform procedure requiring financial assistance to be disbursed within seven days of release.

The court also asked the Centre to consider revising the existing rehabilitation scheme within three months to increase financial assistance and provide “subsistence support” when disbursements are delayed.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh issued a slew of directions while hearing two petitions, including one filed by a bonded labour survivor, highlighting delays in financial assistance and institutional shortcomings in the identification and rehabilitation of those rescued.
The Bench said eradication of bonded labour was a “continuing obligation”, requiring authorities to ensure that those freed were meaningfully rehabilitated.
“The constitutional prohibition against bonded labour and the statutory measures enacted to enforce it cannot remain mere assurances on paper.
The release of a bonded labourer cannot be treated as the completion of the State’s obligation when the conditions necessary for a life of dignity remain unfulfilled.
Identification, release and rehabilitation must therefore be understood as interconnected stages of a continuing constitutional responsibility,” the Bench said.

Taking note of the Union government’s submission that a revised standard operating procedure (SOP) for dealing with cases of bonded labour had been formulated on May 14, the Bench directed all States and Union Territories to implement it within six months.
The Centre was also asked to issue supplementary guidelines, in consultation with the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), within three months.
The Bench said the stipulated procedure should provide for complaints of bonded labour to be verified ordinarily within 24 hours, followed by prompt rescue wherever required.
Once a person is identified a bonded labourer, the competent authority must conduct the necessary inquiry and ordinarily issue a release certificate within 24 hours.

The court also addressed the difficulties faced by bonded labourers rescued outside their States of origin, where lack of coordination between authorities can delay their release and access to rehabilitation benefits.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Censures TN IPS Officer A Arun Over Detention Order, Expunges Madras High Court's Adverse Remarks On Him
stories.title: Supreme Court Censures TN IPS Officer A Arun Over Detention Order, Expunges Madras High Court's Adverse Remarks On Him
stories.summary: An officer holding a senior position in the police administration is expected to appreciate the significance of the duties entrusted to him, the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: An officer holding a senior position in the police administration is expected to appreciate the significance of the duties entrusted to him, the Court said.

Observing that the powers of preventive detention must be exercised with great circumspection by the public authority, the Supreme Court on Monday (November 2) accepted the unconditional apology tendered by a senior IPS officer for an error committed by him while passing a detention order, and not apologizing before the High Court.

The matter arose from a detention order, passed by A. Arun under Section 3(1) of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Cyber Law Offenders, Drug Offenders, Forest Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Sand Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Slum-Grabbers and Video Pirates Act, 1982, classifying the first respondent's father as a “Goonda”.

The detention was based on allegations that the detenue and his wife, who were directors of a real estate company, had cheated a buyer after receiving over ₹1.38 crore towards the purchase of an apartment.

It was alleged that the apartment was not handed over despite execution of the agreements and payment, and that the property was subsequently dealt with in favour of third parties and mortgaged using allegedly forged documents.
A criminal case was registered under Sections 409, 420, 465, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
The detenue and his wife were arrested on September 1, 2025.
The detenue's daughter challenged the detention order before the Madras High Court, which set it aside.
However, while doing so, the High Court made adverse observations against.
A. Arun in its judgment while quashing the detention order.
At the relevant time, the officer was Commissioner of Police, Greater Chennai.
The High Court observed that he was habitual in passing such detention orders.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Allows Certified Green Crackers In Delhi-NCR For Diwali On Nov 7-8; Year-Round Ban To Resume On Nov 9
stories.title: Supreme Court Allows Certified Green Crackers In Delhi-NCR For Diwali On Nov 7-8; Year-Round Ban To Resume On Nov 9
stories.summary: The Court permitted the bursting of firecrackers between 6 AM and 8 PM on November 7, and between 7 AM and 10 PM on November 8.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court permitted the bursting of firecrackers between 6 AM and 8 PM on November 7, and between 7 AM and 10 PM on November 8.

The Supreme Court has permitted the manufacture, sale and bursting of approved green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR for a limited period ahead of Diwali, while directing the restoration of the complete firecracker ban from November 9, 2026.
A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale permitted the bursting of firecrackers between 6 AM and 8 PM on November 7, and between 7 AM and 10 PM on November 8.
The Court also temporarily restored the licences of firecracker traders whose licences had been cancelled, allowing them to sell approved green crackers between November 4 and 6.
The Court has emphasised that the relaxation is temporary and subject to stringent safeguards governing manufacture, sale and use of firecrackers.

It has directed the authorities to ensure that only CSIR-NEERI-approved green crackers were sold and that conventional firecrackers were not allowed to enter the market under the guise of green crackers.
The Court's directions are broadly in line with last year's order which allowed a similar relaxation for Diwali.

In the latest order, the Court emphasised that it not only intends to regulate the upcoming Diwali situation, but also to bring about a holistic change for which public perception regarding firecrackers needs to change.
"Regardless of the directions passed by this Court to regulate the upcoming situation, the endeavour is to bring about a holistic change for which the public perception has to change.
One must embrace the Precautionary Principle by being proactive to prevent issues, instead of merely reacting after they have occurred.

While parting, we wish to make a sincere plea regarding the feasibility of raising awareness by the members of the Bar, prominent personalities, including celebrities and sportspersons, to lend their voice and influence through a voluntary public-awareness campaign.

Such participation can play a significant role in encouraging citizens to celebrate the upcoming festivals in a safe, responsible, and environmentally conscious manner, without causing harm to public health, or aggravating the already precarious air quality", the Court concluded.

stories.headline: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
stories.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
stories.summary: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).
This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government.
A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.

“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement.
The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.
Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi.
Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home.
Nepali diplomatic sources told.
The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here.
India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda.

Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed.
Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.
